title: Ethiopia Border Conflict - Hundreds Flee Into Kenya As Gunfire Reported in Moyale
summary: [Capital FM] Moyale -- Hundreds of Ethiopian nationals, mainly women, children and young people, have crossed into Kenya through Moyale following escalating tensions between regional leaderships in Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions, prompting heightened security surveillance along the border.

title: All of Africa Today - October 28, 2026
summary: [allAfrica]

title: Peace-Security Anchor Ethiopia Must Consolidate Commitments to Peace and Security - Former PM
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia, which remains an anchor for peace and security in the region, must strengthen and continue this genuine commitment to peace, former Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn told ENA.

title: Somaliland Joins Ethiopian Navy's Red Sea Workshop
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Addis Ababa -- Somaliland is among the participants in a four-day regional maritime security workshop hosted by the Ethiopian Navy in Addis Ababa, bringing together naval and maritime representatives from Yemen, Oman, Djibouti and Puntland to strengthen cooperation across the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

title: Ethiopia Working to Become Continental Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, Says Health State Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is striving to become a continental pharmaceutical manufacturing hub by leveraging the African Continental Free Trade Area, regional value chains, regulatory cooperation, and pooled procurement to expand African-made health products and position, Health State Minister Dr. Muluken Argaw said.

title: UN Reports 36,000 Ethiopian Arrivals Fleeing Moyale Conflict, Kenya Rights Commission Urges Aid
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Approximately 36,000 people have crossed from Ethiopia into Kenya to flee conflict in and around Moyale, with food, clean water, shelter, sanitation, and healthcare identified as the most urgent needs, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) in Kenya said.

title: Drone Strikes Kill Couple Fleeing Clinic, Father With Four Children, in Tigray's Medebay Terer
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Two drone strikes in Medebay Terer, Tahtay Koraro woreda in northwestern Tigray, killed seven civilians, including an eight-year-old girl, and injured six others on October 9 and October 21, residents told Addis Standard.

title: Russia, Ethiopia Advance Nuclear Power Talks, Discuss Expanded Flights and Visa Facilitation
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Russia and Ethiopia are coordinating a draft agreement on a nuclear power plant project while discussing expanded air connections and further visa facilitation for tourists and businesspeople, Russian Ambassador Yevgeny Terekhin said, according to the Russian state news agency TASS.

title: Drought, Food Shortages and Child Malnutrition Deepen Humanitarian Needs in Afar, Amhara and Tigray
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Drought, rising food prices, shortages of essential medicines and disruptions to health services are compounding humanitarian needs across northern Ethiopia's Afar, Amhara and Tigray regions, with displaced children particularly vulnerable to acute malnutrition, according to a humanitarian assessment document seen by Addis Standard.

title: Liberation Without Domination - Ethiopia's Opposition Alliance and the Right to Decide
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival, or EPFAS, was announced on 20 September 2026. Announced participants included the Oromo Liberation Front-Oromo Liberation Army, known as OLF-OLA, the Amhara Fano National Movement, and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). Its statement, reproduced on an OLF-OLA-associated website, proposes an inclusive temporary government, temporary governing rules, and public discussion of the country's political futur

title: Ethiopia Delivers Over 1 Million Digital Business Registration, Licensing Services
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia provided more than 1.08 million business registration and licensing services digitally over a three-month period, according to the Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration.

title: ICRC Reaffirms Commitment to Partnership With Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its partnership with Ethiopia, commending the humanitarian efforts of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS).

title: Egypt to Deploy Troops in Somalia Under Bilateral Deal Ahead of Aussom Integration
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Egypt is preparing to deploy troops to Somalia under a bilateral military cooperation agreement before transferring approximately 1,000 personnel into the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), raising concerns over operational coordination and command structures.

title: Ethiopia Calls for Hydro-Diplomacy On Shared Rivers As Egypt's El-Sisi Reiterates Water Security Is a 'Red Line'
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has called for stronger regional cooperation and hydro-diplomacy over shared water resources, while Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi warned that Cairo would not accept any fait accompli that compromises its water security, highlighting the persistent divide between the two countries over the management of the Nile.

title: Holy Synod Confirms 60 Orthodox Faithful Killed in Latest Attacks in Oromia, Calls for Protection, Justice
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church's Holy Synod has confirmed that 60 Orthodox faithful were killed in attacks in two districts of Oromia's Arsi Zone on 20 and 24 October, while more than 20 others sustained severe injuries and 20 homes were burned down, according to a statement issued on Monday.

title: From Strategic Asset to Regional Fault Line - Djibouti At Crossroads of Red Sea Power Struggle
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- For three decades, Djibouti's political economy rested on a simple model: Ethiopia needed Djibouti's ports, and Djibouti needed Ethiopia's trade. Around that relationship, President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh's government built a model based on ports, foreign military bases, strategic infrastructure, and external financing. That arrangement transformed one of Africa's smallest states into one of its most strategically important.

title: Tana Forum Concludes With Call for African Sovereignty, Integration
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa concluded in Bahir Dar with current and former African leaders calling for accelerated regional integration, technological sovereignty and concrete action to address the continent's peace and security challenges.

title: ENDF Chief of Staff Vows to Safeguard Ethiopia's Interests in Abay River, Red Sea
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Chief of Staff of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF), Field Marshal Birhanu Jula, has reaffirmed Ethiopia's commitment to safeguarding its legitimate interests in the Abay River and the Red Sea.

title: Endf At 119 - Advancing Ethiopia's Peace, Regional Stability and Tech Self-Reliance
summary: [ENA] The Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF), marking 119 years of institutional development, represents a longstanding pillar of Ethiopia's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security. From defending the country's independence to participating in international peacekeeping operations and expanding domestic defense manufacturing, the institution has continued to evolve in response to changing national, regional and global security demands.

title: Honorary Defense Members Push for Stronger Commitment to Ethiopia's Red Sea Access
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Honorary members of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) have rallied behind Ethiopia's quest for sovereign Red Sea access.

title: Tana Forum Opens in Ethiopia As African Leaders Debate Security and Economic Sovereignty
summary: [Nile Post] The 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa has opened in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, bringing together African leaders, policymakers and security experts to discuss the continent's peace and security challenges, economic sovereignty and changing geopolitical landscape.

title: At Least 48 Civilians Killed in Weekend Attacks in Ethiopia's Oromia Region, Once Again
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- At least 48 people have been killed and more than 31 others wounded, some severely, in attacks by armed men in Chole and Birbo kebeles of Shirka Woreda, Arsi Zone, in southeastern Oromia, residents who attended the victims' mass funeral told Addis Standard, describing door-to-door killings, looting and the use of heavy weapons.

title: Moyale Clashes Leave Trail of Death, Destruction Across Seven Districts - Tens of Thousands Flee to Kenya
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Fighting triggered by a dispute over the display of the Somali regional state flag in border city Moyale, a city administered by both Oromia and Somali regions, has spread across seven districts over the weekend, leaving a trail of deaths, injuries and property destruction. Tens of thousands have also fled across the border into Kenya seeking safety.

title: Ethiopian Passport Ranks Among World's Lowest, Limiting Travel to 17 Visa-Free Destinations
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Ethiopian passport holders can travel to only 17 countries without a visa, according to figures attributed to the 2026 Global Passport Power Index, highlighting barriers facing Ethiopian citizens seeking international business, education and cultural opportunities.

title: Ethiopia's Transitional Justice Should Resume, but Not Where It Left Off
summary: [ISS] Public consultations on transitional justice laws should start only after National Dialogue recommendations, gaps and new developments have been considered.

title: Ethiopia's Abiy Inaugurates Major Megech Irrigation Dam
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Gondar -- Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project in Gondar, a major infrastructure development aimed at expanding agricultural production, improving water supplies and creating economic opportunities for surrounding communities.

title: PM Abiy Stresses for Stronger Indigenous Capacity to Drive National Development
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has emphasized for stronger domestic institutional and human capacity, improved coordination among government institutions, and the removal of systemic bottlenecks to accelerate Ethiopia's development.

title: Kenya Red Cross Launches Emergency Response for Families Fleeing Moyale Clashes Into Marsabit
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) has launched an emergency response for families arriving in Moyale, in Kenya's Marsabit County, after fleeing insecurity linked to renewed clashes across the border in Ethiopia, as fighting in the disputed border town has forced civilians to seek safety on the Kenyan side.

title: Drone Strikes Kill Schoolchildren in Amhara, Civilians in Tigray Regions As Conflicts Show No Sign of Abating
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Drone strikes in Ethiopia's Amhara and Tigray regions killed schoolchildren and other civilians on Tuesday, 20 October, according to eyewitnesses and local residents who spoke to Addis Standard, adding to mounting civilian casualties amid renewed fighting between federal forces and armed opponents in both regions.
